newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish exports seen to rise 15-17 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turkish exports seen to rise 15-17 pct in 1997.

text.p: A senior Turkish trade official said on Wednesday Turkey's exports were expecetd to rise 15-17 percent in 1997.

"Export records from the beginning of the year until today show show that 1997 exports have entered a rising trend of 15-17 percent," foreign trade undersecretary Osman Dogangun told a meeting organised by the Istanbul Chamber of Industry.
Exports would total $28-28.5 billion in 1997 if existing conditions were maintained, he said.
Dogangun added that the level of exports in January would be revised upwards to around $1.9 billion from the $1.7 billion announced previously.
The State Statistics Institute announced on Wednesday that Turkey's foreign trade deficit rose 49.3 percent in the first nine months of 1996 to $13.978 billion.
Exports in the nine months rose 8.7 percent from a year earlier to $16.564 billion and imports jumped 24.1 percent to $30.541 billion.
The release of Turkish trade data has been delayed by technical difficulties arising from the country's customs union with the European Union which into effect at the start of 1996.
